subject: Ascend launch: commit cadence & discount structure
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightcart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Ascend launch — initial sizing & pricing ask

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the call yesterday — BrightCart is planning a phased launch of our new Ascend recommendation engine in Q4. We expect a small beta in September and full public launch in November. We're trying to map expected token usage and need clear guidance on per-token pricing if we commit to a monthly minimum with step-up tiers as we scale.

High-level forecast (monthly tokens):
- Sept (beta): ~75M tokens
- Oct (ramp): ~350M tokens
- Nov (launch): ~1.2B tokens
- Dec (holiday peak): ~2.0B tokens

Questions we have:
1) Do you offer stepped commit tiers that allow predictable discounts as volume grows each month?
2) Can we true-up after a month if actual usage is higher/lower?
3) How do you handle one-off surge capacity during the launch window (overages vs. burst billing vs. temporary credit)?

Procurement & timeline: legal + procurement need a pricing sheet and an initial SOW this week to get to our finance team. Our procurement contact is procurement@brightcart.com.

Appreciate a proposal or example cadence you typically recommend for launches like this.

Best,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Product
BrightCart

[attachment: launch_forecast.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ascend launch — initial sizing & pricing ask

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear forecast. This is exactly the kind of ramp Redwood is set up to support. I sketched a few approaches below; Monica (cc) will follow up with a formal pricing sheet and a short mutual action plan.

Quick options we commonly recommend for launches with steep seasonality:
- Phased commit with step-up bands: set a conservative initial monthly commit for beta, with automatic planned increases at pre-agreed months (e.g., 75M -> 350M -> 1.25B -> 2B). Discounts escalate with each band.
- Rolling true-up: allow a single monthly true-up to your committed tier (so you only pay commit price for the committed amount and pay overage at discounted band pricing for anything above).
- Surge protection add-on: a fixed reserve of burst capacity priced as a monthly option that you can consume without immediate overage penalties during launch weeks.

I'll attach a short XLSX with an example cadence. Key open items for us to finalize: discount tiers (percent off list per-token), exact commit volumes per month, and the surge cap amount.

Next steps: Monica will send a formal proposal and a 1-pager for procurement. Can you confirm the target signature date (procurement deadline) and whether your finance team requires Net-30 vs Net-45? Also loop in procurement@brightcart.com if you'd like us to include procurement-specific fields in the SOW.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — that framework looks promising. Procurement confirms target signature by 2026-07-05; finance prefers Net-30 but can push to Net-45 with an OK from their director. A couple of clarifying points from my side:

- For the phased commit, we'd prefer monthly commits that step up automatically if our forecast commits to the next band; can Redwood accommodate planned automated step-ups rather than renegotiating each month?
- For true-ups: we need the ability to true-up up to two months after the usage month (so we can reconcile on a monthly cadence but have a 60-day window).
- For surge protection: we'd like a burst pool of 1B tokens for the November launch available for up to two weeks. Does that count toward the monthly commit or is it billed as separate burst usage?

Procurement also asked for examples of previous customers that used stepped monthly commits and a note on how you handle audits for usage reporting (we will need token-level logs).

If you can send a sample table that lays out price per token at each band and the exact mechanics for step-ups/true-ups, we can expedite internal approvals.

Thanks — Elena

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ascend launch — initial sizing & pricing ask

Elena — looping in Monica (pricing) and Marcus (finance) with a concrete proposal and the mutual action plan attached. Below is the high-level phased commit calendar we recommend and the mechanics for step-ups/true-ups. Please review and we can finalize a proposal for signature by 2026-07-05.

Proposed phased commit (monthly):
- Sept (beta): commit 75M tokens @ $0.00012/token (base list $0.00015) — 20% discount
- Oct (ramp): commit 350M tokens @ $0.00010/token — 33% discount
- Nov (launch): commit 1.25B tokens @ $0.000085/token — 43% discount
- Dec (peak): commit 2.0B tokens @ $0.00007/token — 53% discount

Step-up mechanics:
- Automated step-ups: BrightCart provides a signed schedule listing target commits by month. On the first of each month, Redwood will automatically move the committed tier to the next scheduled band if that band is within the signed schedule. No renegotiation needed for planned steps.
- True-up window: 60 days after the usage month (as requested) — overages above the committed amount are billed at the next-tier discounted per-token rate, with a single reconciliation invoice covering the month.
- Surge pool: we can reserve a one-time burst pool (1B tokens) billed as a pre-paid monthly add-on. Tokens consumed from the burst pool count first against the pool; any remainder counts against the monthly commit at the applicable tier. If the pool is fully used, additional overage will follow the true-up rules.

Other items:
- Token-level usage logs are available via our Console (secure link) and will be included with the SOW for audit purposes.
- Payment terms: Net-30 standard; finance (Marcus) said Net-45 can be accommodated for the initial quarter with an approved PO.

Attachments: RDW-Proposal-Ascend-Commits.pdf (proposal excerpt), MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (milestones + procurement fields), preliminary_pricing.xlsx (detailed bands). Also included HubSpot deal link and a DocuSign prepare link for the proposal.

Can procurement confirm the billing contact and the exact PO number so Marcus can set up the account? If everything looks good we can issue an initial SOW and start the DocuSign flow today.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
